not_material.rationale: Aluminium in honey is low natural/environmental background. The best modern reference-method source (naccari2025, ICP-MS, n=38) measures honey Al at 4.5-6.0 mg/kg, consistent with the wider literature (typical 0.1-5 mg/kg; country maxima ~29). The pooled p97 of ~152 mg/kg is a method-inflation artifact, not ubiquitous mineral content: the pool is dominated by an ICP-OES source (tomczyk2020) and reconstruction tails, and honey is not among EFSA's high-Al foods. No credible regulator sets an aluminium ML for honey; dietary Al is TWI-managed. The pool requires reference-method restriction (logged as an outstanding item); the not-material determination rests on the ~5 mg/kg reference value, not the inflated 152.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Al ML for honey in any jurisdiction; real ICP-MS occurrence ~5 mg/kg (pool p97 method-inflated)
not_material.jurisdictions_checked: EU 2023/915 (no Al); Codex; FSANZ; EFSA; JECFA

not_material.rationale: Hexavalent chromium does not persist in the infant-formula matrix. Two independent modern reference-method studies find it absent: saraiva2021 (species-specific isotope-dilution HPLC-ICP-MS, LOQ 0.049 ug/kg) does not quantify Cr-VI in infant formula and measures near-total reduction of spiked Cr-VI to Cr-III during sample prep; hernandez2019 (ANSES LC-ICP-MS, 68 brands of milk/dairy/cereal) detects no Cr-VI and attributes older positive findings to analytical artifacts. The sole source reporting measurable Cr-VI (soares2000, superseded ion-exchange/ETAAS, 37x coarser LOQ) is graded EF-3 context-only. See data/workbench/standards/2026-07-31-chromium-formula-adjudication.md. China GB 2762 regulates total Cr only, not Cr-VI.
not_material.regulatory_basis: No Cr-VI ML for infant formula in any jurisdiction (China GB 2762 Table 7 is total Cr); reference-method non-detection

not_material.rationale: Aluminium in salt derives from permitted anti-caking additives, not contamination. In the US, sodium aluminosilicate is GRAS as an anti-caking agent in table salt up to 2% (21 CFR 182.2727). In the EU most aluminium-silicate anti-caking additives were removed for consumer protection by Reg (EU) 380/2012 (E556/E558/E559 banned from 2014; E554/E555 restricted to non-salt uses), so EU table salt carries little additive Al. Dietary aluminium is managed by intake against the EFSA TWI (1 mg/kg bw/week) and JECFA PTWI (2 mg/kg bw/week) with additive use-level controls, not by per-food contaminant MLs; oral bioavailability from food is ~0.1-0.3%. No credible regulator sets an aluminium contaminant ML for salt. The single pooled datum (n=1, 164 mg/kg) cannot distinguish additive from natural background.
